title: Speculative KV prefetch safety buffer and headroom ledger for mixed-priority continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As continuous batching scales across mixed-priority tenants, speculative KV cache prefetch (to reduce cold-KV misses) increases transient activation and KV allocations on GPU. We need a controlled mechanism to allow optimistic prefetch while guaranteeing a predictable headroom buffer for weights + activations so we avoid cross-tenant OOMs and P99 latency regressions.

Problem statement: Current prefetch logic is all-or-nothing and can push memory usage above soft safety bands when many tenants issue concurrent interactive requests. This leads to noisy preemptions, evictions, and occasionally degraded latency for high-priority requests. There is no fine-grained accounting that ties speculative KV prefetch to a recoverable budget and no graceful admission control that reconciles steady-state batching with transient prefetch spikes.

Goal: Implement a "safety buffer ledger" that budgets speculative KV prefetch per-tenant (and per-priority lane), enforces a minimum headroom reservation for weights+activations, and integrates with the continuous-batching admission controller and eviction policies. The ledger should support: per-tenant soft budget, overcommit shadowing with fast reclaim, telemetry hooks for budget burn-rate, and a conservative fallback that disables speculative prefetch when headroom approaches the safety threshold.
proposal: 1) Introduce a lightweight per-tenant prefetch ledger kept in serving runtime (memory-accounting component). Each ledger entry tracks: speculative_kv_allocated, speculative_kv_peak, last_burn_rate, and reserved_headroom_stamp. 2) When a request triggers speculative KV prefetch, the runtime consults the ledger to decide allowed prefetch size. If speculative_kv_allocated + requested_prefetch > soft_budget, allow up to soft_budget + transient_slack where transient_slack is small fraction tied to global headroom. 3) Reserve a min_headroom quota per-GPU that is never allocated to speculative prefetch; admission controller refuses prefetch if global free memory <= min_headroom. 4) Implement a fast-reclaim path: if memory pressure is detected, speculative KV is the first candidate for asynchronous eviction (de-prioritized to weights/active KV entries). 5) Add metrics: per-tenant prefetch_budget, prefetch_used, prefetch_reclaims, headroom_available. 6) Expose opt-in flags (runtime config) to gate per-tenant budgets and a global overly-conservative mode to disable speculative prefetch for multi-tenant clusters during high-stress windows.
acceptance_criteria: No increase in P99 token latency for P0 tenant traffic under representative mixed-priority replay (<= 1% relative),
Under synthetic multi-tenant stress (100 concurrent tenants), total speculative KV usage must remain within 110% of configured soft budgets and reclaim events must complete within 150ms median,
System must never allocate below min_headroom reservation (verify with unit/integration tests that attempt to force overcommit),
Telemetry shows prefetch budget accounting, burn rates, and reclaims on canary cluster after rollout
Config toggle to fully disable speculative prefetch works and is tested via CI gate
milestones: Integration with admission controller + canary perf tests (2026-03-10)
implementation_notes:
- Keep ledger in per-GPU shared memory region with lock-free increment/decrement (atomic) where possible; fall back to shard-by-tenant locks for rare operations.
- Prefer async prefetch eviction paths that do not block the serving thread: schedule reclamation work to background worker with priority hint.
- Integrate with existing KV LRU hooks: speculative entries tagged and scored lower for eviction.
- Admission controller needs a fast path: if headroom_available <= min_headroom, reject prefetch authorization.
- Add a debug dump that prints ledger state per-GPU for support debugging (controlled by runtime flag).
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for ledger accounting (increments, concurrent prefetch attempts).
2) Microbench: synthetic workload that issues controlled prefetch sizes to validate slack behavior and reclaim latency.
3) Replay test against production traffic snapshot for mixed priorities to ensure P99 regression < 1%.
4) Chaos test: artificially reduce available GPU memory and assert fast-reclaim behavior and no weight eviction.
5) End-to-end canary with observability checks and automated rollback if reclaim SLOs violated.
rollout_plan:
- Feature gated runtime flag.
- Canary on one cluster with low-risk workloads (select tenants) for 48h. Monitor prefetch burn-rate and headroom graphs.
- Expand to 25% of clusters for 72h. If we observe increased reclaim latency or P99 regressions, automatically toggle conservative mode that caps transient_slack to zero.
- Full rollout after 1-week stable canaries and signoff from SRE and runtime performance team.
comments: 2026-02-11 Aisha Patel: Initial triage complete. Scope: ledger + admission controller + telemetry. Linked ENG-220017 as dependency for improved memory sensors.

2026-02-18 Jonah Kim: Prototype ledger implemented in branch runtime/prefetch-ledger. Basic unit tests pass; starting stress runs against small cluster. Observed typical reclaim median ~120ms under synthetic bursts.

2026-02-24 Performance team (review): Suggested adding per-priority lane throttles and limiting transient_slack to 5% by default. Also requested additional telemetry (per-tenant reclaim latency histogram).
2026-02-27 Jonah Kim: Integrated per-priority lane caps and added reclaim histograms. Running replay test against last-week production snapshot. Initial P99 delta +0.6% — within target.

2026-03-02 QA: Found race during rapid parallel prefetch attempts causing ledger briefly report negative available due to ordering; fixed by switching to atomic compare-and-add. Added unit test covering tight loops.
2026-03-04 SRE signoff pending: Need to validate canary on a cluster with heterogeneous GPU types (A100, H100). Blocked until ENG-468999 telemetry tagging for GPU family is available.
